title: Satan the Tempter
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Satan the tempter seeks to draw people away from trust and obedience to God by distorting truth, appealing to sinful desire, and presenting rebellion as life.
summary: Satan the tempter seeks to draw people away from trust and obedience to God by distorting truth, appealing to sinful desire, and presenting rebellion as life.
christFocus: Jesus Christ resisted Satan’s temptation with perfect obedience and the written Word. He is the faithful Savior who succeeds where sinners fail and helps His people stand against temptation.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Satan tempts by questioning God’s Word, goodness, authority, and promises. In Eden, he deceived by twisting what God had said and presenting sin as wisdom and freedom.

Jesus faced temptation in the wilderness and answered with Scripture. Unlike Adam and unlike all sinners, Christ remained faithful under testing and refused to worship, serve, or trust anything above the Father.

Temptation also works through disordered desire. Satan may entice, but people are responsible when they are drawn away by their own desires. Scripture refuses both denial of evil and evasion of responsibility.

Believers resist temptation by truth, prayer, watchfulness, and dependence on Christ. The tempter is real, but he is not sovereign, and God provides grace for His people to stand.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Temptation often feels persuasive because it promises relief, control, pleasure, identity, or escape. This doctrine exposes temptation as deception that leads toward death.

It also gives hope. Jesus has faced temptation without sin, and He helps His people in their weakness. Believers do not fight temptation alone.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Resist temptation early and truthfully. Do not negotiate with lies, hide in secrecy, or trust your own strength. Answer temptation with Scripture, flee what feeds sin, pray for help, and look to Christ, who is faithful in every place you are weak.
